p.src: Now Lady Wu saw that Sun Quan remained hesitant and undecided, so she said to him, “My late elder sister left these words: ‘As Bofu lay dying, he said: When domestic affairs are in doubt, consult Zhang Zhao; when foreign affairs are in doubt, consult Zhou Yu.’ Why do you not summon Gongjin now and ask his counsel?” Sun Quan was delighted and at once sent a messenger to Poyang to invite Zhou Yu to deliberate upon the matter. As it happened, Zhou Yu had been drilling the naval forces on Lake Poyang. When he heard that Cao Cao’s great army had reached the Han River, he hastened back by night to Chaisang Commandery to discuss military affairs. Before the messenger could depart, Zhou Yu had already arrived. Lu Su, who was on the closest terms with Zhou Yu, went first to meet him and related all that had happened in full detail. Zhou Yu said, “Zijing, do not worry. I have a plan of my own. Go quickly now and invite Kongming to see me.”

p.src: Lu Su mounted his horse and left. Only then did Zhou Yu settle down to rest. Suddenly it was reported that Zhang Zhao, Gu Yong, Zhang Hong, and Bu Zhi had come to call upon him. Zhou Yu received them in the hall, and when all were seated and the customary greetings had been exchanged, Zhang Zhao said, “Does the Commander understand what is at stake for Jiangdong?” Zhou Yu replied, “I do not.” Zhang Zhao said, “Cao Cao commands a host of a million and is encamped along the Han River. Yesterday his proclamation arrived here, inviting our lord to join him in a hunt at Jiangxia. Though he intends to swallow us up, he has not yet revealed it openly. We have urged our lord to submit for the present, in hopes of sparing Jiangdong from disaster. But unexpectedly Lu Zijing brought Liu Bei’s military adviser Zhuge Liang here from Jiangxia. Wishing to avenge his own wrongs, Zhuge Liang has deliberately employed persuasive words to provoke our lord. Zijing, meanwhile, clings obstinately to his error and will not see reason. We have been waiting for the Commander to settle the matter once and for all.” Zhou Yu asked, “Are all your views the same?” Gu Yong and the others replied, “We are all of one opinion.” Zhou Yu said, “I too have long wished to submit. Please return home for now. When I see our lord tomorrow morning, a firm decision shall be made.”

p.src: Zhang Zhao and the others took their leave. Shortly afterward, it was reported that Cheng Pu, Huang Gai, Han Dang, and a company of fighting generals had come to see him. Zhou Yu welcomed them in and exchanged greetings with each of them. Cheng Pu said, “Does the Commander know that sooner or later Jiangdong will belong to another?” Zhou Yu replied, “I do not.” Cheng Pu said, “We have followed General Sun since the founding of his enterprise and fought hundreds of battles, great and small, before finally winning the cities of six commanderies. Now our lord listens to the civil counselors and means to surrender to Cao Cao. This is truly a shameful and lamentable thing. We would rather die than suffer such disgrace. We beg the Commander to urge our lord to resolve upon raising arms. We are ready to fight to the death.” Zhou Yu asked, “Are all you generals of the same opinion?” Huang Gai sprang up in fury, struck his forehead with his hand, and cried, “My head may be severed, but I swear I will never surrender to Cao!” They all said, “None of us is willing to submit.” Zhou Yu said, “I myself mean to fight Cao Cao to the finish; how could I consent to surrender? Please return home, generals. When I see our lord, a firm decision shall be made.”

Bofu’s dying injunction entrusted foreign affairs to you, General. Now we are counting on you to preserve the state and stand as its sure support, firm as Mount Tai. With your heroic ability, General, and the formidable defenses of Eastern Wu, Cao Cao may not so easily achieve his desire.”

p.src: As the two argued back and forth, Kongming merely folded his hands in his sleeves and smiled coldly. Zhou Yu asked, “Why do you smile, Master?” Kongming replied, “I am not laughing at anyone else. I laugh only because Zijing fails to understand the times.” Lu Su said, “Why, sir, do you in turn laugh at me for failing to understand the times?” Kongming replied, “Gongjin’s intention to submit to Cao Cao is entirely reasonable.” Zhou Yu said, “Kongming is indeed a man who understands the times; surely he shares my mind.” Lu Su said, “Kongming, how can you say such a thing as well?” Kongming replied, “Cao Cao is supremely skilled in the use of arms, and none beneath Heaven dares withstand him. Formerly only Lü Bu, Yuan Shao, Yuan Shu, and Liu Biao dared oppose him. Now all of them have been destroyed by Cao Cao, and no one remains in the realm. Only Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, fails to understand the times and stubbornly contends with him. Now he is isolated at Jiangxia, with his very survival uncertain. If you firmly resolve to submit to Cao Cao, General, you can preserve your wife and children and retain your wealth and rank. As for the transfer of the imperial destiny, leave that to Heaven’s decree. Why should it be regretted?”

p.src: Lu Su grew furious and cried, “Would you have my lord bend his knee and suffer humiliation before a traitor to the state?” Kongming replied, “I have a humble plan. It will not require leading sheep and bearing wine, yielding territory, or presenting the seals of office; nor need our lord cross the river in person. You need only dispatch a single envoy to convey two persons in a small boat to Cao Cao’s camp on the river. If Cao Cao obtains these two, his host of a million will all cast off their armor, roll up their banners, and withdraw.” Zhou Yu asked, “What two persons could make Cao Cao’s army withdraw?” Kongming replied, “For Jiangdong to lose these two would be like a great tree losing a single drifting leaf, or a vast granary losing one grain of millet. But if Cao Cao obtains them, he will surely be overjoyed and depart.”

He has long heard that Lord Qiao of Jiangdong has two daughters, the elder named Da Qiao and the younger Xiao Qiao, whose beauty could make fish sink and wild geese fall, shame the moon, and cause flowers to hide. Cao Cao once swore: ‘My first wish is to pacify all within the Four Seas and establish an imperial enterprise; my second is to obtain the two Qiaos of Jiangdong and place them upon the Bronze Bird Terrace to delight my later years. Why do you not seek out Lord Qiao, General, purchase his two daughters for a thousand pieces of gold, and send someone to present them to Cao Cao? Once Cao Cao obtains the two women, his every desire will be satisfied, and he will surely withdraw his army. This is the very stratagem by which Fan Li presented Xi Shi. Why not carry it out at once?”

p.src: When Zhou Yu had heard it, he flew into a rage, sprang from his seat, pointed north, and cursed: “The old villain has insulted me beyond endurance!” Kongming hurriedly rose to restrain him, saying, “In former times, when the Chanyu repeatedly invaded the frontier, the Han emperor promised him a princess in marriage to secure peace. Why begrudge Cao Cao two common women now?” Zhou Yu said, “There is something you do not know. The elder Qiao is the wife of General Sun Bofu, and the younger Qiao is my own wife.” Kongming pretended to be alarmed and said, “I truly did not know. I spoke recklessly and deserve death! I deserve death!” Zhou Yu said, “The old villain and I swear never to coexist!” Kongming said, “The matter should be considered thrice, lest you later regret it.” Zhou Yu said, “Bofu entrusted his cause to me. How could I abase myself and surrender to Cao Cao? What I said just now was only meant to test you. From the moment I left Poyang Lake, I intended to march north. Though axe and blade were laid upon my neck, I would not change my resolve. I hope you will lend me your strength so that together we may defeat Cao Cao.” Kongming said, “If you do not disdain my service, I shall gladly labor for you like a faithful hound or horse and stand ready at all times to obey your commands.” Zhou Yu said, “Tomorrow I shall see my lord, and we will at once discuss raising the army.” Kongming and Lu Su took their leave, then parted and went their separate ways.

p.src: Before long, Zhou Yu entered for an audience. When the formal courtesies and Sun Quan’s inquiries after his welfare were over, Zhou Yu said, “I recently heard that Cao Cao has led his army to encamp along the Han River and sent a dispatch here. What is your lordship’s judgment?” Sun Quan handed Zhou Yu the proclamation. After reading it, Zhou Yu laughed and said, “The old villain thinks Jiangdong has no men of worth. How dare he insult us so!” Sun Quan asked, “What is your opinion?” Zhou Yu said, “Has my lord discussed the matter with the civil and military officers?” Sun Quan said, “We have debated it for several days. Some urge me to surrender, and others urge me to fight. My mind remains undecided, so I have asked Gongjin to settle the question.” Zhou Yu asked, “Who has urged my lord to surrender?” Sun Quan replied, “Zhang Zibu and the others all favor that course.” Zhou Yu then asked Zhang Zhao, “Sir, I should like to hear why you advocate surrender.” Zhang Zhao said, “Cao Cao holds the emperor in his power and campaigns throughout the realm, always acting in the name of the imperial court; now he has also taken Jingzhou, and his might has grown still greater. The only thing by which our Jiangdong can resist him is the Yangtze River. But now Cao Cao possesses not merely hundreds but thousands of warships. If he advances by land and water together, how can we withstand him? It would be better to surrender for the present and devise another plan afterward.” Zhou Yu said, “That is the argument of a pedantic scholar! Since Jiangdong’s realm was founded, it has now passed through three generations. How could we bear to cast it away in a single day?” Sun Quan asked, “If so, what plan should we adopt?”

p.src: Zhou Yu said, “Though Cao Cao claims the title of Han chancellor, in truth he is a traitor to the Han. General, with your divine martial prowess and heroic gifts, you have inherited the achievements of your father and brother and hold Jiangdong, with crack troops and ample provisions. You should now range boldly across the empire, removing cruelty and violence for the state. How could you surrender to a traitor? Moreover, Cao Cao’s present campaign violates many principles of warfare. The north is not yet pacified, and Ma Teng and Han Sui remain a threat behind him, yet Cao Cao has undertaken a prolonged southern campaign: that is his first disadvantage. His northern troops are unskilled in naval warfare, yet Cao Cao has abandoned saddle and horse, trusting instead to boats and oars to contend with Eastern Wu: that is his second disadvantage. Furthermore, it is the bitter cold of midwinter, when there is no fresh fodder for the horses: that is his third disadvantage. He has driven soldiers from the central plains on a long journey through rivers and lakes; unaccustomed to the climate and terrain, many will fall ill: that is his fourth disadvantage. Cao Cao’s army suffers from all these disadvantages; however numerous it may be, it is certain to lose. The time for you to capture Cao Cao is now. Grant me several thousand picked troops and let me advance to garrison Xiakou; I shall defeat him for you!”

Your counsel that we should attack accords perfectly with my own intent. I fear only that you may waver in uncertainty.” Sun Quan drew his sword and hacked a corner from the writing table before him, saying, “Any civil or military officer who again speaks of surrendering to Cao Cao shall share the fate of this table!” Having spoken, he bestowed the sword upon Zhou Yu and appointed him Commander-in-Chief, Cheng Pu Deputy Commander, and Lu Su Colonel Who Assists the Army. Should any civil or military officer disobey orders, Zhou Yu was to execute him with that sword.

The old villain and I swear never to coexist!

p.src: Zhou Yu received the sword and addressed the assembly: “By my lord’s command, I shall lead the forces against Cao Cao. Tomorrow, every general and official shall come to the field headquarters by the river to receive orders. Anyone who is late or causes delay shall be dealt with according to the Seven Prohibitions and Fifty-Four Capital Offenses.” With that, he took leave of Sun Quan, rose, and departed from the palace. The civil and military officials dispersed without a word.

p.src: When Zhou Yu returned to his lodgings, he immediately invited Kongming to discuss affairs. Kongming arrived. Zhou Yu said, “Today the council at my lord’s palace reached its decision. I ask you now for a sound plan to defeat Cao Cao.” Kongming said, “General Sun’s heart is not yet steady, so no decisive strategy can be made.” Zhou Yu asked, “What do you mean that his heart is not steady?” Kongming replied, “He is afraid of the size of Cao Cao’s army and fears that the few cannot withstand the many. You must explain the troop numbers to him and dispel his doubts completely; only then can the great enterprise succeed.” Zhou Yu said, “Your judgment is excellent.”

p.src: He then went back to see Sun Quan. Sun Quan said, “Gongjin, your coming at night must mean there is some urgent matter.” Zhou Yu asked, “When the troops are assigned tomorrow, will my lord have any misgivings?” Sun Quan replied, “I worry only that Cao Cao’s troops are numerous and that the few cannot withstand the many. I have no other doubts.” Zhou Yu smiled and said, “That is precisely why I have come, to set my lord’s mind at ease. Because Cao Cao’s proclamation claimed a million troops by land and water, my lord became doubtful and afraid without examining whether the claim was true or false. Let us now reckon the true figures: the troops he brings from the central plains number no more than one hundred fifty or sixty thousand, and they are already exhausted by long campaigning; the forces he acquired from the Yuan clan number only seventy or eighty thousand, and many of them remain suspicious and unsubdued. Though their numbers may be great, an army of long-weary soldiers commanding a host of doubtful allegiance is nothing to fear. With fifty thousand troops, I shall be fully able to defeat him. I beg my lord not to be troubled by this.” Sun Quan stroked Zhou Yu’s back and said, “Gongjin, these words are enough to dispel my doubts. Zibu is devoid of strategy and has deeply disappointed me. Only you and Zijing are of one heart with me. You, Zijing, and Cheng Pu may select the troops today and advance at once. I shall dispatch further troops behind you, laden with abundant supplies, to reinforce you. If your vanguard should fare badly, return to me. I shall then personally fight a decisive battle with the traitor Cao. I have no further doubts.”

p.src: Zhou Yu thanked him and withdrew, thinking secretly, “Kongming had already fathomed the Marquis of Wu’s heart. His schemes are a step beyond my own. In time he will surely become a danger to Jiangdong. Better to kill him.” That very night he sent for Lu Su to come to his tent and told him of his desire to kill Kongming. Lu Su said, “You must not. Before the traitor Cao has been defeated, to kill a worthy man would be to deprive ourselves of an ally.” Zhou Yu said, “This man serves Liu Bei and will surely become a danger to Jiangdong.” Lu Su said, “Zhuge Jin is his elder brother. Why not have him persuade Kongming to enter the service of Eastern Wu? Would that not be excellent?” Zhou Yu approved his suggestion.

p.src: At dawn the next day, Zhou Yu went to the field headquarters, entered the central command tent, and took the high seat. Executioners bearing swords and axes stood on either side, while civil officials and military commanders assembled to receive his orders. Now Cheng Pu was older than Zhou Yu, yet Zhou Yu presently held the higher rank, which displeased him; that day he therefore pleaded illness and stayed away, sending his eldest son, Cheng Zi, in his place. Zhou Yu addressed the commanders: “The law of the realm favors no one. Each of you must faithfully discharge his office. Cao Cao now usurps power even more outrageously than Dong Zhuo: he holds the Emperor captive in Xuchang and masses brutal troops upon our borders. I have now received orders to punish him, and I trust that you will all strive valiantly forward. Wherever the army passes, the people must not be molested. Merit shall be rewarded and crimes punished, without favoritism or indulgence.”

p.src: When he had finished issuing his commands, he appointed Han Dang and Huang Gai as vanguard commanders of the first division. They were to lead the warships under their command, depart that very day, proceed to the mouth of the Three Rivers, establish a camp, and await further orders; Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai were assigned to the second division; Ling Tong and Pan Zhang to the third; Taishi Ci and Lü Meng to the fourth; Lu Xun and Dong Xi to the fifth; and Lü Fan and Zhu Zhi were appointed roving inspectors in all directions. They were to urge on and supervise the officers and men of all six divisions, advancing by land and water and assembling by the appointed date.

p.src: Once the assignments were complete, the commanders each prepared their ships and weapons and set out. Cheng Zi returned to his father, Cheng Pu, and told him that Zhou Yu had deployed the troops with perfect discipline in every action. Cheng Pu was greatly startled. “I have always scorned young Zhou as weak and unfit to command; but to act as he has today—he is a true commander indeed! How could I refuse to submit to him?” He then went personally to the field headquarters to apologize. Zhou Yu courteously apologized in return.

p.src: The next day, Zhou Yu summoned Zhuge Jin and said, “Your younger brother Kongming possesses the talent to assist a king. Why should he demean himself by serving Liu Bei? Now that he has fortunately come to the Southland, I would ask you, sir, to spare no words in persuading him to leave Liu Bei and serve Eastern Wu. Our lord would thereby gain an able assistant, while you brothers would be reunited. Would that not be splendid? I pray you go to him at once.” Zhuge Jin replied, “Since coming to the Southland, I am ashamed to have rendered not the slightest service. Now that the Commander-in-Chief has given me this charge, how could I fail to exert myself?” He mounted at once and rode straight to the posthouse to see Kongming. Kongming welcomed him inside. The brothers wept and bowed to each other, each speaking of his feelings during their long separation.

p.src: With tears in his eyes, Zhuge Jin said, “Brother, do you know of Boyi and Shuqi?” Kongming thought to himself, “Young Zhou must have sent him to persuade me.” He therefore answered, “Boyi and Shuqi were sages and worthies of ancient times.” Zhuge Jin said, “Though Boyi and Shuqi ultimately starved to death beneath Mount Shouyang, the two brothers remained together. You and I were born of the same parents and nursed at the same breast, yet now we serve different lords and cannot be together morning and evening. Compared with Boyi and Shuqi, can we feel no shame?” Kongming replied, “What you speak of, elder brother, is affection; what I uphold is righteousness. You and I are both men of Han. Imperial Uncle Liu is a scion of the Han house. If you would leave Eastern Wu and join me in serving the Imperial Uncle, you would neither shame your duty as a servant of Han nor be kept apart from your own flesh and blood. Thus both affection and righteousness would be fulfilled. What do you think of this, elder brother?”

p.src: Zhuge Jin thought, “I came to persuade him, only to be persuaded by him instead.” Unable to make any reply, he rose and took his leave. Returning to Zhou Yu, he recounted Kongming’s words in detail. Zhou Yu asked, “What do you think?” Zhuge Jin replied, “I have received General Sun’s profound favor. How could I ever betray him?” Zhou Yu said, “Since you are resolved to serve your lord loyally, nothing more need be said. I have a plan of my own to bring Kongming to submission.” And so it was said:
